title: Ordered lexer rules need grammar boundaries and native controls
applies_when: A first-match regex lexer misclassifies a clause keyword before a parenthesis, or splits a documented multi-character operator so formatting inserts whitespace inside it.
lesson: Reproduce with the real tokenizer and parser, then identify the first matching rule rather than adding a downstream grouping or output workaround. For sqlparse JOIN(subquery), move compound JOIN recognition ahead of the generic function-name lookahead but retain dotted-name guards. For PostgreSQL pattern operators, recognize the four documented star-suffixed comparisons before the generic comparison prefix; do not add '*' to a broad operator character class. Pair complete SQL with spaced/unspaced forms, inspect tokens and groups, and preserve ordinary functions, qualified identifiers, multiplication, wildcards and quoted text. Whitespace or a comment between symbols is a lexical boundary, not permission to fuse them. Run the same regressions against original and repaired imports plus the native suite.
avoid_when: Do not reserve every keyword before '(' or merge every punctuation run: dialect functions, custom operators and placeholders need separate contracts. sqlparse is non-validating; malformed SQL acceptance is not itself a defect. Current source already handles some cases in old issues: '<@' works on the pinned base even though issue 613 reports otherwise. Read existing PR hunks to distinguish complementary changes from duplicates. Local lexer/formatter checks do not prove database execution, all dialects, other-platform CI, performance or upstream acceptance.

evidence.note: Public no-space JOIN example and discussion distinguish clause tokenization from broader keyword/function questions.
Pinned baseline places the generic function-name lookahead before JOIN recognition, while dotted-name guards precede both.

Open Ready proposal moves the existing rule, with 10 native parser/function/qualified-name controls. The unchanged baseline fails 2 controls; the patch passes all 10 and the 516-test suite, retaining its existing xfail/xpass outcomes. Local correctness evidence, not maintainer acceptance.
Documents ~*, !~*, ~~* and !~~* as case-insensitive regex/LIKE operators; this is a syntax contract, not a sqlparse performance result.

Ready proposal recognizes those four comparisons as complete tokens. Identical native Windows/Python 3.14 tests give original 13 failures and 4 passes versus repaired 17 passes; repaired full suite 523 passes with existing xfail/xpass unchanged. 64 formatting controls preserve lexical tokens and are idempotent. Independent of PR920's JSON-path operator change; not maintainer acceptance.
